sections.title: Interview answer
sections.content:
Go uses `ExecContext` for statements that do not return rows, `QueryContext` for a result set, and `QueryRowContext` for one expected row. `Scan` copies selected columns into destination variables in the same order.

Query arguments travel separately from SQL text through placeholders. A multi-row query returns `*sql.Rows`; code loops with `Next`, scans each current row, closes the cursor, and checks `rows.Err()` for errors that happened during iteration.

For example, `SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE active = $1` can pass `true` as an argument, then scan each row into `int64` and `string`. A nullable nickname needs `sql.NullString`, a pointer, or a query that supplies a non-null value.

Placeholder syntax is driver-specific, and arguments can replace values but not trusted SQL identifiers such as table or column names. A query returning many rows also needs limits or streaming logic so memory and response time remain controlled.

Use direct queries when SQL shape, joins, selected columns, and database behaviour should remain explicit. Select only needed columns and scan into types that correctly represent database values, including nullable columns.

sections.title: The core model: executing and scanning SQL in Go
sections.content:
executing and scanning SQL in Go is easiest to understand by following the data or control from input to result. The details below form one connected model rather than a list of unrelated rules.

A database query has two contracts. The SQL contract defines which rows and columns may come back; the Go contract defines how those values enter typed variables. Keeping the `SELECT` list explicit makes that boundary reviewable. For one row, `QueryRowContext` delays any query error until `Scan`, including `sql.ErrNoRows`. For several rows, `Next` advances the cursor and `Scan` reads only the current row. An error can occur after some rows have been returned, which is why the final `rows.Err()` check matters. Context cancellation bounds waiting and network work, but the exact driver and database determine how cancellation is carried out. Values belong in query arguments. If a user chooses a sort column, the program must map that choice to a small allow-list of trusted identifiers instead of trying to bind the name as a parameter.
